Installing Janus

The installers and packages for Windows, Linux and macOS: what each one puts on your computer, and how to open Janus from a terminal.

On this page

  1. Windows
  2. Linux x86_64
  3. macOS (Apple Silicon)
Install Usage Architecture Building README

Windows

Run janus-<version>-setup.exe. It installs per user (no administrator prompt), bundles GDAL (no Python or conda needed: Zeit is part of the program), adds a Start menu entry and, optionally:

  • adds jn to PATH, so you can call it from any terminal (only the install folder's bin, which holds jn.com alone: none of the DLLs Janus carries, GDAL, PROJ, curl, sqlite..., is on PATH, where conda environments, R or QGIS would load them in place of their own);
  • adds Open in Janus to the right-click menu of folders and .tif files;
  • creates a desktop shortcut.

Installing 1.0 over an older version removes the Python runtime the versions up to 0.39 carried; settings, layouts, labels and caches are kept and read as they are.

Up to 1.7 the installer put the install folder itself on PATH, DLLs and all, and a conda environment's Python could then fail to import rasterio or GDAL (ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _warp: The specified procedure could not be found). Installing a newer version replaces that entry with bin; uninstalling removes both.

Linux x86_64

Extract janus-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.xz anywhere and run jn from that folder (e.g. ~/apps/janus-<version>/jn serie.tif, or link it into ~/.local/bin). The archive is portable: it carries GDAL and its libraries and the PROJ/GDAL data; only glibc, the graphics drivers (Vulkan, or OpenGL) and X11 or Wayland come from the system. janus.desktop and janus.png are included for a menu entry. File dialogs go through the desktop's portal (xdg-desktop-portal); the Files panel works without it. Data lives in ~/.local/share/janus, caches in ~/.cache/janus. The basemap's tiles are downloaded over https with the system's CA certificates (/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt and the like; the archive carries a copy in share/ssl for systems without one; CURL_CA_BUNDLE overrides both).

macOS (Apple Silicon)

Open janus-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg and drag Janus into Applications. The app carries GDAL and its libraries and the PROJ/GDAL data (macOS 15 or later). Folders and rasters can be opened by dropping them on the window, from the File menu and the Files panel, or from a terminal after linking the program once:

ln -s /Applications/Janus.app/Contents/MacOS/janus ~/.local/bin/jn   # or /usr/local/bin

The app is not signed with an Apple Developer ID: the first time, macOS says it cannot verify the developer. Open it once with right click → Open (or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security), or clear the download's quarantine flag with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Janus.app. Data lives in ~/Library/Application Support/Janus, the overview cache in ~/Library/Caches/Janus.

Installers and packages are built from this repository (see Building); every tagged version publishes the three of them on the Releases page (GitHub Actions, .github/workflows/build.yml).

This page is made from docs/install.md; to change it, change that file.

Built in Rust with egui, wgpu and GDAL. Direct3D 12 on Windows, Vulkan on Linux, Metal on macOS.
